meta.defaultTitle: Help Lito. In memory of Lito Sousa (1967–2026)
meta.defaultDescription: An independent memorial to Lito Sousa, aviation educator and creator of Aviões e Músicas, who died on 1 October 2026 from Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease. His story, his YouTube channel and verified information about prion disease research. Not a fundraiser.

hero.title: Lito Sousa
hero.quoteTranslation: Turbulence doesn't bring a plane down.
hero.quoteNote: The line he repeated to anyone afraid of flying.
hero.lead: Lito spent decades explaining the sky to millions of people. In August 2026 he was diagnosed with Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease. Six weeks later he died in São Paulo, at 59. We lost Lito. This site is what remains of the effort to help him.
hero.portraitAlt: Portrait of Lito Sousa, smiling, arms crossed, wearing a dark sweater.

who.title: Thirty-seven years of making the sky make sense.
who.p1: Lito Sousa was a Brazilian aviation professional. Born in Natal, in Rio Grande do Norte, he started as an aircraft mechanic in commercial aviation. He later became a pilot and built experience across generations of aircraft. He specialized in Human Factors and Safety, the discipline that studies how people and complex systems fail together, and how to keep them from failing.
who.p2: Then he did something unusual for a technician: he taught the public. Through Aviões e Músicas, one of the largest aviation education platforms in Brazil, he spent more than fifteen years turning dense technical knowledge into something anyone could follow. Turbulence. Engines. Why a wing works. Why an accident happened, and what changed afterward.
who.p3: Along the way he helped thousands of people overcome their fear of flying, trained new professionals, and became a reference for an entire generation that learned aviation through his voice.
who.imageAlt: Lito Sousa in a safety vest and an A350 visitor cap, smiling inside an aircraft assembly hall, with an airliner fuselage behind him.
who.imageCaption: Lito on a visit to an aircraft assembly line

diagnosis.title: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, in sixty seconds.
diagnosis.intro: CJD is a rare, rapidly progressive, neurodegenerative prion disease. It is not an infection in the usual sense and it is not a cancer. It involves a protein in the brain folding into the wrong shape.

normal.title: A normal protein
normal.body: Every person makes prion protein (PrP). In its normal shape it is harmless.

misfold.title: Misfolding
misfold.body: In CJD, some PrP takes on an abnormal shape that the body cannot easily clear.

chain.title: A chain reaction
chain.body: Abnormal PrP induces normal PrP to misfold too. The process spreads through brain tissue.

damage.title: Neurological damage
damage.body: Nerve cells are lost. Coordination, vision, memory, speech and movement decline, often within months.

diagnosis.noTreatment: According to public health authorities, there is currently no proven treatment that stops or reverses the disease.
diagnosis.noContagion: Ordinary social contact does not transmit sporadic CJD. Family members and people interacting normally with a patient are not at increased risk.

timeline.title: An attempt to buy time.
timeline.p1: When the family made the diagnosis public, it was clear the disease would not leave time to look for answers slowly. Help Lito started two days later as an independent initiative, to organize verified information and bring researchers, physicians and institutions to Lito's official team.
timeline.p2: The project never asked for money and never spoke for the family. With Lito's death on 1 October 2026, the effort to help him ended. The site stays online as a memorial until the domain expires.
timeline.imageAlt: Lito Sousa and his wife Mila Seidl embracing and smiling, both in white shirts, at an outdoor event.

researchers.title: Research did not arrive in time for Lito. It may still arrive for others.
researchers.body: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease still has no proven treatment. Until the domain expires, this site is a starting point for anyone working on prion disease: what was known, who does the research and where to look. The references are kept as they were while the site was trying to help Lito, and they are no longer updated.

keepAlive.title: Keep Lito's channel on the air.
keepAlive.p1: Lito's work did not end with him. There are more than fifteen years of videos on Aviões e Músicas, and a team that still looks after the channel. While he was ill, his friends organized to keep it active, because there are families that depend on it.
keepAlive.p2: The family comes first. The best way to support Mila Seidl and their son is to keep what Lito built alive, and to respect their grief.

aboutLitoPage.title: A mechanic who learned to explain the sky.
aboutLitoPage.lead: Lito Sousa (Joselito Geraldo de Sousa, 1967–2026) was a Brazilian aviation professional, educator, content creator, speaker, pilot, internationally experienced aircraft mechanic and Human Factors and Safety specialist. He is remembered above all as the creator and face of Aviões e Músicas.

career.title: The career
career.body: Lito was born in Natal, Rio Grande do Norte, on 25 January 1967. According to the official Aviões e Músicas channels, he had more than 37 years of experience in commercial aviation. His career began in aircraft maintenance, where he gained hands-on experience across generations of aircraft. He later became a pilot and specialized in Human Factors and Safety, the field that studies how human performance, procedures and technology interact in high-risk operations.

education.title: The educator
education.body: For more than fifteen years, Lito made aviation easier for the public to understand. Aviões e Músicas became one of the largest aviation education platforms in Brazil by doing something simple and hard at the same time: taking technical content seriously while speaking plainly. Accident analyses, systems explanations, cockpit procedures and the reasoning behind safety rules became content that pilots, mechanics, enthusiasts and nervous passengers can follow. He also wrote the book Onde Morrem os Aviões.

impact.title: The impact
impact.body: Lito helped thousands of people overcome their fear of flying. He had a short line for them: "turbulência não derruba avião", turbulence doesn't bring a plane down. He contributed to aviation education and professional training, and opened doors for new professionals entering the field. For a generation of Brazilians, aviation has his voice.

why.title: Why this site exists
why.body: This site began as an attempt to connect Lito's case with the people who study the disease. Today it is a memorial. The same clarity he brought to aviation is what the project tries to keep: information that is organized, verified and accessible.

farewell.title: The farewell
farewell.body: In August 2026, the family made his Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease diagnosis public. Lito died in São Paulo on 1 October 2026, at 59. He is survived by his wife, Mila Seidl, and their son. His videos remain on the Aviões e Músicas channel.

cjdPage.title: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, explained carefully.
cjdPage.lead: This page explains what CJD is, why it is so hard, and why time matters. It is written for families, journalists and curious visitors first, with deeper detail available for professionals. It is not medical advice.

what.title: What is CJD?
what.body: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (in Portuguese, Doença de Creutzfeldt-Jakob, DCJ) is a rare, rapidly progressive, neurodegenerative disease. It belongs to a family called prion diseases. The disease involves the prion protein, which every person makes, adopting an abnormal shape that spreads through the brain and damages nerve cells. Most cases are sporadic, meaning they occur without a known cause. Smaller proportions are genetic or acquired.
what.technical: CJD is a transmissible spongiform encephalopathy caused by the conformational conversion of cellular prion protein (PrP^C) into a misfolded, aggregation-prone isoform (PrP^Sc). Sporadic CJD accounts for roughly 85% of cases, genetic forms for 10 to 15%, and acquired forms (iatrogenic, variant) for a small minority. Subtypes are classified by PRNP codon 129 genotype and PrP^Sc glycotype.

prion.title: What does "prion disease" mean?
prion.body: A prion is a protein that has misfolded in a way that causes other copies of the same protein to misfold too. The word comes from "proteinaceous infectious particle". Unlike bacteria or viruses, there is no genetic material involved in the spread of the abnormal shape inside the brain. That is part of why prion diseases are so difficult: the thing causing damage is a version of something the body normally makes.

difficult.title: Why is it difficult?
difficult.body: CJD is rare, so most physicians see very few cases. Its early symptoms overlap with many other conditions, including encephalitis, autoimmune disorders, strokes and other dementias. Diagnosis usually requires a combination of clinical assessment, MRI, EEG, and tests on cerebrospinal fluid. Because the disease moves quickly, the window in which a diagnosis can be confirmed and options evaluated is short.
difficult.technical: Supportive tests include DWI/FLAIR MRI showing cortical ribboning or basal ganglia signal, periodic sharp wave complexes on EEG, and CSF markers such as 14-3-3, total tau and, with high specificity, RT-QuIC. Definitive diagnosis is neuropathological.

time.title: Why does time matter?
time.body: CJD typically progresses over months. Patients lose coordination, vision, memory, speech and movement. Public health authorities state that there is currently no proven treatment capable of stopping or reversing the disease. Every week matters for care decisions, for understanding the available research, and for any conversation with a specialized team.

contact.title: Can you catch it from someone?
contact.body: No. Sporadic CJD is not spread by ordinary social contact. Family members, caregivers and people interacting normally with a patient are not at increased risk because of everyday contact. Standard precautions are used in specific medical settings, such as neurosurgery, but this has nothing to do with being near a person.

research.title: What research is happening?
research.body: A small, specialized research community has spent years on prion disease. Work includes reducing the amount of normal prion protein in the brain with RNA-targeting therapies, better biomarkers for earlier diagnosis, and methods to track how the disease progresses. One PrP-targeting siRNA is now in a first-in-human safety study. This is early-stage research, not an available treatment.

aboutPage.title: What Help Lito is, who is responsible for it, and what it is not.
aboutPage.lead: Help Lito is an independent public-interest initiative created by Bruno Silva. It started as a way to connect verified scientific information with Lito's team during his illness. After his death in October 2026, it became a memorial. The responsible person is named here for accountability, not promotion.
aboutPage.sourceCodePending: The repository link will be published here once available.

why.title: Why this site exists
why.body: When a rare, fast disease strikes a public figure, information scatters. Rumors, well-meant but unverified suggestions and fraudulent campaigns appear within days. Help Lito was created in August 2026 to close that gap: one place that explained who Lito was, what CJD is, where research happens and how a professional could reach his official team.

memorial.title: Why it became a memorial
memorial.body: Lito died on 1 October 2026. The request for help with his case no longer applies, but the disease still has no proven treatment. The site now keeps his memory, points to the videos he left and keeps prion disease research in view. The form that prepared messages for Lito's team has been removed.

notFundraising.title: Not a fundraising campaign
notFundraising.body: Help Lito does not accept donations. There is no crowdfunding, no PIX, no cryptocurrency, no payment processing and no financial support section of any kind. The official team has warned that fraudulent fundraising campaigns are using Lito's name. If you see a financial campaign claiming to represent Help Lito or Lito without confirmation from his official channels, treat it with caution.

independent.title: An independent initiative
independent.body: Help Lito is not run by Lito's family, by Mila Seidl, by Aviões e Músicas or by any hospital, university or research organization, and it has no official affiliation with any of them. It does not represent the Broad Institute, MIT, Harvard or any institution mentioned on this site. Institutions appear for information only.

responsibility.title: Who is responsible
responsibility.body: This website was created and is maintained by Bruno Silva, independently and at his own expense. There is no organization behind it. The purpose of naming a responsible person is simple: if something on this site is wrong, harmful, or unwanted by the people it concerns, there must be someone who answers for it. That person can be reached at helplito@brunosilva.io.

curation.title: How information is curated
curation.body: Medical and research content comes from public health authorities, official clinical trial registries and peer-reviewed literature. Every source is listed on the Sources page with an access date. A trial's status can change at any time; the site shows the date of the last check and always links to the official registry. Information about Lito is limited to what the family, the team and the press made public.

noGuarantee.title: No guarantees
noGuarantee.body: No treatment or study described on this site guarantees eligibility or benefit. Nothing here claims that any experimental therapy works.

notAdvice.title: Not medical advice
notAdvice.body: This site does not provide medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Decisions about care belong to patients, families and their physicians.

corrections.title: Corrections and removal
corrections.body: Anyone can request a correction. Lito's family, his official team, Aviões e Músicas or any person or institution mentioned on this site can ask for content to be changed or removed. Write to helplito@brunosilva.io. Requests from the family take priority over everything else.

handover.title: Ownership and handover
handover.body: Help Lito was created to help, not to control the narrative around Lito's life. If the family, the official team, Aviões e Músicas or another authorized party wants to discuss the administration, ownership, operation or removal of this site and domain, that conversation is welcome at helplito@brunosilva.io. This does not mean ownership transfers automatically; it means the door is open.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.body: The source code of this website is published openly to support transparency, review and independent collaboration. Anyone can inspect how the site works, what it collects, and how content is structured. This is an accountability measure, not a showcase.

ending.title: When the site goes offline
ending.body: The helplito.org domain was registered on 23 August 2026 for one year, paid for by the person responsible for the site. When it expires on 23 August 2027, the site goes offline. The source code and the research log stay public on GitHub. Lito's videos stay on the Aviões e Músicas channel.

sections.title: No medical advice
body: Nothing on this site should be used as a substitute for consultation with qualified healthcare professionals. If you or someone you care for is facing a medical emergency, contact local emergency services.

sections.title: Accuracy and change
body: Medical information is summarized from public health authorities, official clinical trial registries and peer-reviewed literature. We try to keep it accurate and current, but science and trial status change. Always consult the original source, linked on the Sources page.

sections.title: No endorsement, no eligibility
body: References to research, clinical trials, institutions or organizations do not constitute endorsement, partnership or recommendation. No statement on this site implies that any patient is eligible for, or will benefit from, any study or therapy.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: Help Lito collects as little as possible. This page describes exactly what the current implementation does.

sections.title: Browsing
body: The site does not use advertising trackers, analytics scripts or third-party embeds. No account exists and no cookie is set for personalization. If the hosting platform provides aggregate, privacy-respecting traffic measurement in the future, this page will be updated to say so.

sections.title: Language preference
body: When you switch languages, a cookie may store your choice so the site remembers it on the next visit. It contains only the language code.

sections.title: No contact form
body: The site has no contact form. The form that used to live on the Can You Help? page was removed after Lito's death. It never stored data: it built an email on your device that you sent yourself.
No page on this site stores user data.

sections.title: Email you send us
body: If you write to helplito@brunosilva.io, your message is kept only as long as needed to reply or act on it, and it is not shared with anyone.

sections.title: Your rights
body: If you believe Help Lito holds any information about you, or you want something removed, write to helplito@brunosilva.io.

responsibleUse.title: Responsible Use
responsibleUse.lead: How this site is meant to be used, what its information can and cannot do, and how to ask for changes.

sections.title: Purpose
body: Help Lito is an independent memorial to Lito Sousa and a public record about Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease and prion disease research. It is not a fundraiser and not a medical service.

sections.title: Where the information comes from
body: Content is curated from public, official, scientific and institutional sources: public health authorities, clinical trial registries, peer-reviewed literature, Lito's official channels and press coverage. Every source is listed on the Sources page with an access date.

sections.title: Information can become outdated
body: Science moves, and clinical trial availability changes. Recruitment status shown on this site is always paired with a last verified date and a link to the official registry. Check the original record before acting on anything.

sections.title: Not advice, not a recommendation
body: Help Lito does not provide medical advice and does not guarantee eligibility for any treatment or study. Nothing on this site should be read as a recommendation of a treatment. Decisions belong to patients, families and their physicians.

sections.title: Respect the family and the institutions
body: Do not send treatment suggestions, speculation, opinions about the care he received or commercial offers to the family, to Lito's team or to the institutions listed here.

Do not organize or join mass messaging toward researchers, hospitals or institutions listed on this site. They appear here so professionals can verify them, not so the public can contact them on Lito's behalf.

sections.title: Images and the family's privacy
body: Do not reproduce the photographs on this site outside their context, and never next to sensational or misleading text, tributes included. Share only what the family chose to make public.

sections.title: No fundraising in Lito's name
body: Fraudulent campaigns using Lito's name were reported during his illness. Help Lito does not and will not ask for money. Do not start fundraisers in Lito's name.

sections.title: Corrections, removal and contact
body: Anyone can request a correction. Lito's family, his official team, Aviões e Músicas or any person or institution mentioned here can ask for content to be changed or removed, and can raise questions about the administration or future of the site. Write to helplito@brunosilva.io.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.lead: This is a public-interest website. Accessibility is part of its purpose, not polish.

sections.title: Standards
body: Help Lito aims to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA. Pages use semantic HTML, visible focus states, sufficient color contrast, descriptive alt text for every image, and keyboard-accessible navigation.

sections.title: Motion and reading
body: The site contains no decorative animation. Transitions are limited to hover and focus states, and respect the prefers-reduced-motion setting. Headings use Georgia, a widely available serif; body text uses a sans-serif at comfortable sizes.

sections.title: Languages
body: The site is available in English and Brazilian Portuguese, and each page declares its language for assistive technology.

sections.title: Report a barrier
body: If you encounter a barrier, write to helplito@brunosilva.io with "accessibility" in the subject line.
